land.text: the Serb-majority districts of Croatia, 17,028 km2 at the greatest extent in 1991 (infobox): northern Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun and Banovina, then western and eastern Slavonia

predecessors.note: Croatia was a republic of the Yugoslav federation until June 1991; Cliopatria's Croatia row starts in 1992.

land.text: Western Slavonia retaken in Operation Flash (1-4 May 1995) and the Krajina in Operation Storm (4-7 August 1995), 'about 10,400 km2'

successors.note: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia passed to a UN transitional administration (UNTAES, from 15 January 1996) and were formally returned to Croatia in 1998 (page).

capitals.name: Knin
capitals.note: Infobox capital Knin; Glina was an autonomous district, not the capital. Coordinates are Knin's.

rulers.name: Milan Babić
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Infobox: Babić 1991-1992, Hadžić 1992-1994, Martić 1994-1995; Babić's administration announced the SAO Krajina on 21 December 1990. Replaced by Goran Hadžić on 26 February 1992.

rulers.name: Goran Hadžić
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Succeeded by Martić, who took office on 26 January 1994.

correction.text: the SAO Krajina, the Serb districts of northern Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun and Banovina (about 10,100 km2 at the grid; the pages give no boundary)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Four circles (Knin 32 km, Lika 36 km at 15.85 E 44.55 N, Kordun 22 km at 15.70 E 45.28 N, Banovina 25 km at 16.15 E 45.38 N) stand in for the districts because Natural Earth's counties are far larger and the gazetteer lacks Gračac, Korenica, Glina and Slunj; the circle total matches the 10,400 km2 that Croatia retook in Operation Storm. The SAO Krajina of December 1990 had no recognised boundary.

correction.text: the Republic of Serbian Krajina at its greatest extent: the Krajina, Western Slavonia (from December 1991) and Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia (from 26 February 1992); 17,028 km2 in the infobox

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The shape is about 13,700 km2 at the grid against the infobox 17,028 km2 (ratio 0.80, within the factor of two); the missing part is the unmapped edge of the Krajina and Banovina. The three UN Protected Areas (Vance plan, January 1992) froze the line to May 1995.

correction.text: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia: all that remained after Operation Flash (May) and Operation Storm (August), until the Erdut Agreement of 12 November 1995

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the end of the year. Western Slavonia went on 1-4 May and the Krajina on 4-7 August; the remnant passed to UNTAES administration in January 1996 (page).

region.text: the Serb districts of Croatia around Knin, Lika, Kordun and Banovina

ledger.note: 21 December 1990: the Serb districts of Croatia announce the SAO Krajina. 'Babić's administration announced the Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Krajina (SAO Krajina)' on 21 December 1990, after the Log Revolution (17 August 1990 in the infobox) and an August referendum on 'sovereignty and autonomy' (99.7%). The page names no boundary.

August 1991: the war for the Krajina begins. 'A wider-scale war began' in August 1991 and 'large numbers of Croats were expelled'. The SAO had declared on 1 April 1991 that it would secede from Croatia after a 16 March 1991 referendum (99.8%) on joining Serbia.
19 December 1991: the Republic of Serbian Krajina is proclaimed. 'SAO Krajina and SAO Western Slavonia proclaimed the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and its constitution took effect.'

region.text: Western Slavonia around Pakrac and Okučani, the SAO Western Slavonia

ledger.note: 19 December 1991: SAO Western Slavonia joins. The two oblasts proclaimed the republic together.

region.text: the Serb-held districts of Croatia, now three UN Protected Areas

ledger.note: January 1992: the Sarajevo Agreement ceasefire freezes the front. 'The Sarajevo Agreement, a ceasefire, was signed' in January 1992 (month only); the UN Security Council authorised UNPROFOR to protect the UN Protected Areas on 21 February 1992, under the Vance plan signed in November 1991.

region.text: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia, the Danube border with Serbia

ledger.note: 26 February 1992: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia join. 'SAO Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia joined the RSK.' Milan Babić was replaced as president by Goran Hadžić the same day.

1 May 1995: Operation Flash. Operation Flash retook the RSK's Western Slavonia, 'taking full control of the territory by 4 May, three days after the battle began' (Operation Storm page; the Krajina page says only May 1995).
4 May 1995: Operation Flash ends with all of Western Slavonia in Croatian hands.
May 1995: Western Slavonia is lost. Croatia 'retook all RSK territory in western Slavonia' within four days.

region.text: the Krajina: northern Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun and Banovina

ledger.note: 4 August 1995: Operation Storm begins. 'Operation Storm commenced at dawn on 4 August 1995'; the 7th Guards Brigade entered Knin on 5 August with little resistance; on 4 August RSK authorities ordered the evacuation of Northern Dalmatia and Lika, on 6 August of Glina and Vrginmost.
7 August 1995: Operation Storm is declared complete 'on the evening of 7 August'; mop-up continued to 14 August. The Krajina page says Operation Storm 'overran most of the RSK' on 8 August.
August 1995: the Krajina is lost. Croatia regained about 10,400 km2 and 'around 150,000-200,000 Serbs of the area formerly held by the ARSK had fled'.

region.text: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia, the last of the RSK, under UN transitional administration

ledger.note: 12 November 1995: the Erdut Agreement ends the Republic. It was signed on 12 November 1995 for the Serb side by Milan Milanović; UNTAES began overseeing the reintegration of Eastern Slavonia into Croatia on 15 January 1996 and the territory was returned to Croatia in 1998. The land in between is held by the UN, so the counterpart is nobody.

wars.name: Croatian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Ceasefire in January 1992 with UN Protected Areas; Croatia retook Western Slavonia (Operation Flash, May 1995) and the Krajina (Operation Storm, August 1995); Eastern Slavonia passed to UNTAES (1996-1998) and back to Croatia.
wars.note: The RSK page does not name the war; the title is the usual English one. The JNA formally withdrew from Croatia in May 1992 but left much equipment to the RSK forces (page).

wars.name: Operation Flash
wars.outcome: Croatia took all of Western Slavonia by 4 May 1995.

wars.name: Operation Storm
wars.outcome: Croatia regained about 10,400 km2 in four days (4-7 August 1995); 150,000-200,000 Serbs fled.
wars.note: The Z-4 Plan was presented on 30 January 1995 and rejected by both sides; Geneva talks of 3 August 1995 failed.

certainty.note: A front line frozen by the January 1992 ceasefire and the UN Protected Areas, not a border; the pages give no municipal boundaries, so the cells follow circles.

sources.title: Republic of Serbian Krajina

sources.title: Operation Storm
sources.note: Operation Flash 1-4 May 1995, Operation Storm 4-7 August 1995, 10,400 km2, Vance plan, Z-4 plan.

notes: Requested by the eu-22 scope (the Yugoslav war fronts). Modelled as a rebel state (rule 5). Not settled: the boundary of the SAOs (the gazetteer lacks Gračac, Korenica, Glina, Slunj, Pakrac, Okučani and Vojnić as places, so circles are used), the Union with Republika Srpska (the page gives no date for a 'United Serbian Republic', only mid-1993), the Autonomous Districts of Glina and Knin (30 December 1992, never functioned), the East and West UN sectors (the Storm page is silent), the UNTAES years and the 1998 return of Eastern Slavonia (outside this dossier: the Croatian dossier needs a gain from nobody in 1998). The Storm page's 56,500 km2 'implied' RSK area is not used. Counterpart republic-of-croatia has a Cliopatria row only from 1992.
